newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 15.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
* The Secretary of the U.S. Air Force may be willing to allow the nation's first female B-52 pilot, who is under fire for adultery charges, to resign with an honourable discharge.
* Russia has agreed to a Clinton Administration plan to bring into the fold of the NATO military alliance the former Central European satellites of Moscow.
* The decision to extend NATO to former Soviet-bloc countries is perhaps the United States' most significant foreign policy initiative since the end of the Cold War.
* The New Jersey Supreme Court, as it has three times before over three decades, ruled that the state's school financing plan is unconstitutional.
* The U.S. House of Representatives voted to provide public housing to more of the working poor. The change is designed to reverse the trend of housing projects being ghettos of unemployed.

* A top lawyer in the firm that had filed Yankees owner George Steinbrenner's lawsuit against Major League Baseball has resigned, saying he wanted to represent clients whose interests collide with the large companies the firm represented.
* More and more college fraternities are moving to ban alcohol, threatening the party atmosphere stirred by their forefathers.
